source.title: Sparse Autoencoder Decomposition of Clinical Sequence Model Representations: Feature Complexity, Task Specialisation, and Mortality Prediction
source.authors: Chris Sainsbury; Feng Dong; Andreas Karwath

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE reconstruction quality and tests SAE-feature interventions, but does not test whether the reconstruction error is linearly predictable, how per-token errors scale across SAE sizes, whether reconstruction errors are pathological relative to matched random errors, or whether the error term carries function.
record.gate_note: The explained-variance results directly measure SAE reconstruction quality and are recorded below, but they do not measure the error properties named in V1–V6. The warfarin→INR perturbation experiments ablate SAE features, not the SAE error term; they are recorded as related results under fits_no_version. Mortality-prediction comparisons and feature-complexity results are not results about dark matter or its predicted properties.
record.test_reason: The study is not aimed at dark matter and never cites the original, but two of its results bear on versions in a new setting, a 14.5M-parameter clinical sequence model. First, a dictionary-size sweep (Supp. Table S3) shows reconstruction error barely shrinking from 4× to 16× expansion (V2's 'does not vanish with scale'). Second, its delta-mode experiment shows that replacing activations with the full SAE reconstruction, which drops the error term, adds about 86× more noise to the downstream causal estimate than keeping the error (V5). Neither result is in the rows, so the verdicts rest on the text. All recorded rows (per-layer EV, feature ablations) correctly link to no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is too narrow. The authors conclude several things: SAE features show progressive abstraction from token detectors at layer 0 to distributed concepts at layer 6, and EV follows a U-curve with its trough at layer 6. Under full-sequence probes, SAE features beat dense representations for mortality but lose for length of stay. At leakage-safe windows, dense matches or beats SAE on every dataset. Delta-mode intervention cuts the perturbation noise floor about 86×, but feature perturbations stay non-significant. Feature reproducibility across seeds is 21%. They draw no explicit conclusion about SAE error structure.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains TopK SAEs on clinical-sequence-model residual activations and evaluates representation properties and clinical tasks; it does not implement a method for testing dark-matter structure.
record.method_sensitivity: Explained variance varies by layer and dataset. The authors report that K dominates explained variance in the INSPECT layer-6 hyperparameter sweep, while expansion has minimal effect beyond 4×; these settings do not test the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: EV follows a layer U-curve with a layer-6 trough (INSPECT 0.848, MIMIC-IV 0.895).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction fidelity varies with layer depth, lowest at middle-late layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Targeted high-INR latent ablations exceed the random mean in 3 of 4 conditions, but none falls outside the random distribution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-feature ablations give suggestive, non-significant causal effects in this pipeline.

fits_no_version.finding: At leakage-safe windows, SAE-feature probes underperform dense activations for mortality (MIMIC-IV 48h 0.836 vs 0.914, below the bag-of-tokens 0.864).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Information discarded by SAE encoding can carry downstream predictive signal. This is probe-level, not error-term analysis.

record.code_released: https://github.com/csainsbury/ascend-flat (currently private; contact the corresponding author for collaborator access)
record.problems: The study uses one 14.5-million-parameter model. Feature perturbation results are not formally significant, and the authors note limited random-control sets (10–20 per experiment). Feature stability across seeds is 21%; downstream seed-wise variability was not formally quantified. These limitations concern the study's SAE results, but it does not directly test the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No results were left out from the directly relevant SAE reconstruction-fidelity sweep or the related feature-perturbation experiments. Mortality-probe results, feature-complexity analyses, and other clinical prediction results were not extracted because they do not measure the SAE error properties in V1–V6.

untested.parts: All: no regression of the error on the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes; whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts. Only aggregate EV across expansion 4/8/16 is reported.
All: no comparison of reconstruction-induced loss against random errors of equal norm.
All: no split of the error into linear and nonlinear components.
No architecture or end-to-end comparison. The K sweep (EV 0.67→0.94 as K rises 8→32) only shows the sparsity–reconstruction trade-off, not whether dark matter is a training artifact.
Circuit analyses and steering-share measures; only one perturbation pipeline (warfarin→INR) is tested.

missing.what: EV across expansion 4/8/16 at K=8/16/32 (e.g. K=16: 0.842/0.848/0.851), showing error persisting with dictionary size
Noise floor of the downstream DiD estimate in reconstruct mode (±0.43) versus delta mode, which keeps the error (±0.005); about 86× reduction

record.verdict_notes: Both verdicts come from results the rows do not capture, in one small non-language model, and the authors never frame them in dark-matter terms. The V2 evidence spans only a 4× size range at one layer. The V5 evidence is a noise-floor comparison, not a measured share of behaviour lost. Weight both as weak.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of the SAE error vector is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error persists with SAE scale.
Whether SAE-reconstruction replacement harms model loss more than random errors of the same size.
Whether the predictable component holds unlearned features and the nonlinear component is qualitatively different or resists further dictionary learning.
Circuit analyses and steering-share measures; only one perturbation pipeline (warfarin→INR) is tested.
Whether dark matter mostly results from SAE training choices and shrinks with improved architectures or end-to-end training.

relationships.condition: FlatASCEND INSPECT layer 6, TopK K=16, expansion 4×/8×/16× (1,536–6,144 latents)
relationships.reason: Per Supp. Table S3 text, not in rows: EV rises only 0.842→0.848→0.851 as the dictionary quadruples, so the error persists with size. The authors say expansion has 'minimal effect beyond 4×'. This covers a small size range only.
relationships.display_finding: Explained variance rose only from 0.842 to 0.848 to 0.851 as dictionary size quadrupled, leaving persistent reconstruction error.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: FlatASCEND INSPECT layer 6, TopK K=16, expansion 4×/8×/16× (1,536–6,144 latents)
source_check.reason: Supplementary Table S3 gives EV 0.842, 0.848 and 0.851 at the stated expansions and K. This supports persistent aggregate error over this finite sweep; per-token predictability, shared failure contexts and an asymptotic floor remain untested.

relationships.condition: FlatASCEND warfarin→INR perturbation pipeline, SAE at layer 6/9
relationships.reason: Per Section 2.4/4.4 text, not in rows: full reconstruction (error dropped) gives a noise floor of ±0.43 odds-ratio units versus ±0.005 when the error is kept (delta mode). Omitting the error thus swamps feature-level effects. The authors blame this floor for their non-significant perturbation results.
relationships.display_finding: Full reconstruction produced a noise floor of ±0.43 odds-ratio units versus ±0.005 when retaining the error, overwhelming feature effects and contributing to statistically nonsignificant perturbation results.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: FlatASCEND warfarin→INR perturbation pipeline, SAE at layer 6/9
source_check.reason: Sections 2.4 and 4.4 report intervention noise falling from ±0.43 to ±0.005 odds-ratio units when delta mode preserves the original activation plus the decoded modification. Reconstruction noise dominates single-feature intervention signals. This supports a functional analysis cost from discarding error, without measuring a recovered fraction of behavior.

relation.reason: The study's own reconstruction sweep and intervention comparison bear on V2 and V5, despite not targeting dark matter explicitly.

tranche.reason: A clinical-sequence model provides a new setting with results on finite-width reconstruction scaling and the downstream effects of dropping reconstruction error.

source_check.notes: Both verdicts rely on text results absent from the listed rows. Code is reported as hosted in a private repository requiring collaborator access; the perturbation effects are not formally significant.
